details: AstroTrainee is an interactive space mission training platform and simulation game developed using JavaScript, Node.js, Express, MongoDB Atlas, and type script to train junior astronauts in planetary and orbital survival. The project addresses the challenges of making complex space exploration education engaging and preventing system failures during live demonstrations by gamifying life-support mechanics and utilizing robust fallback protocols that ensure uninterrupted gameplay and contextual dialogue even if external services fail. This is important because it bridges the gap in space science education while providing high system reliability and offline resilience for high-stakes simulations and live presentations. The platform works by tracking real-time suit telemetry and orbital hazards through a secure backend while an onboard AI guide named ARIA analyzes incoming metrics and responds with tactical feedback across simulated mission stages. Its main benefits include immersive learning, system resilience, and secure state management backed by robust user authentication. The intended impact is to make space science and survival mechanics accessible and engaging for students while inspiring the next generation of space enthusiasts. The project demonstrates creativity by blending hard technical constraints with narrative gameplay and introducing intelligent wrappers that bridge custom AI endpoints with deterministic fallback logic. Throughout development, the team carefully considered reliability under pressure, performance, scalability, and an intuitive user experience to balance complex telemetry meters.
